description: Dashboard foundation: CSS design tokens, TypeScript types, mock data, shared components (Sidebar, Topbar, StatusBadge, StatCard), and the dashboard layout + root redirect. This FEAT must be complete before FEAT-002 or FEAT-003 can build pages on top of it.
steps: 1. Add `--db-*` CSS design tokens to `app/globals.css` inside the existing `:root` block (after the --ob-* tokens). Tokens: --db-sidebar-bg: #111110; --db-sidebar-text: #a8a29e; --db-sidebar-active: #ffffff; --db-sidebar-w: 240px; --db-topbar-h: 56px; --db-surface: #ffffff; --db-bg: #f5f4f2; --db-primary: #1a1a1a; --db-secondary: #6b6560; --db-accent: #3d6b4f; --db-border: #e8e4df; --db-muted: #f1ede8; --db-danger: #dc2626; --db-warning: #d97706; --db-success: #16a34a.

2. Create `app/dashboard/types/index.ts` with these exported types: BookingStatus (union), StaffRole (union), Hotel, Reservation, RoomType, InventoryDay, RoomInventory, StaffMember, RevenueDay, PayoutTransaction. See dashboard-plan.md for exact type shapes.

3. Create `app/dashboard/mock/data.ts`. Export: MOCK_HOTEL (Hotel), MOCK_RESERVATIONS (Reservation[], at least 12 entries mixing all statuses), MOCK_ROOM_TYPES (RoomType[], 4 types: Deluxe King/Executive Suite/Standard Double/Family Room), MOCK_INVENTORY (RoomInventory[], 4 room types × 30 days), MOCK_STAFF (StaffMember[], 6 members with varied roles/statuses), MOCK_REVENUE_DAYS (RevenueDay[], 30 days realistic Nigerian hotel figures), MOCK_PAYOUTS (PayoutTransaction[], 10 entries). All amounts in NGN (naira). Use realistic Nigerian hotel names and guest names.

4. Create `app/dashboard/components/StatusBadge.tsx` — 'use client'. Props: `{ status: BookingStatus }`. Render a small pill/badge. Color map: pending→amber, confirmed→blue, checked_in→green, checked_out→stone, cancelled→red, no_show→orange. Use inline style with --db-* vars for border/text, Tailwind for layout.

5. Create `app/dashboard/components/StatCard.tsx` — 'use client'. Props: `{ label: string; value: string; delta?: string; deltaPositive?: boolean; icon?: React.ReactNode }`. Renders a clean metric card: label on top, large value, optional delta with up/down arrow and color. Use var(--db-surface) background, var(--db-border) border, var(--db-primary) for value.

6. Create `app/dashboard/components/DashboardSidebar.tsx` — 'use client'. Uses `usePathname()` from 'next/navigation' to highlight active nav item. Nav items (label + href): Overview /dashboard/overview, Reservations /dashboard/reservations, Calendar /dashboard/inventory, Rooms /dashboard/rooms, Guests /dashboard/guests, Analytics /dashboard/analytics, Hotel Profile /dashboard/profile, Staff /dashboard/staff, Subscription /dashboard/subscription, Payouts /dashboard/payouts. Top: HotelOS logo (same style as onboarding sidebar). Bottom: hotel name from MOCK_HOTEL. Each nav item: inline SVG icon (keep icons simple — use basic geometric SVGs), label. Active: white text on slightly lighter dark bg. Inactive: --db-sidebar-text. Sidebar bg: var(--db-sidebar-bg). Width on desktop: 240px, sticky full-height. On mobile: hidden (toggle handled by topbar). No third-party icon library.

7. Create `app/dashboard/components/DashboardTopbar.tsx` — 'use client'. Props: `{ onMenuToggle: () => void }`. Shows: hamburger button (mobile only, calls onMenuToggle), page title derived from `usePathname()`, hotel name chip, notification bell SVG button, user avatar circle with initials. Bg: var(--db-surface), border-bottom: var(--db-border), height: var(--db-topbar-h).

8. Create `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` — server component (no 'use client'). Props: `{ children: React.ReactNode }`. Wraps with DashboardSidebarWrapper (a thin 'use client' wrapper that holds the mobile open/close state and passes onMenuToggle to the topbar). Layout: full-height flex row: sidebar (hidden on mobile, visible lg+) + right column (topbar + scrollable main). Background: var(--db-bg). Export metadata: `{ title: 'Hotel OS — Dashboard' }`.
9. Create `app/dashboard/page.tsx` — server component. Does `import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; redirect('/dashboard/overview');`. This is the entry point redirect.
acceptance_criteria: `npx next build` completes with zero TypeScript errors.
/dashboard and /dashboard/overview appear in the built route list.
DashboardSidebar renders all 10 nav items and highlights the active one using usePathname.
StatCard accepts all its props without TypeScript errors.
StatusBadge renders distinct colors for all 6 booking statuses.
--db-* CSS tokens are present in globals.css and do not conflict with --ob-* tokens.
verification: cd c:\Users\Pkaka\Music\hotel-os && npx next build 2>&1 — expect '✓ Compiled successfully' and zero errors
npx next build 2>&1 | Select-String 'dashboard' — expect /dashboard and /dashboard/overview in output
findings: 1) layout.tsx is a server component; mobile state lives in DashboardSidebarWrapper ('use client'). 2) `app/dashboard/overview/page.tsx` stub created as a placeholder — FEAT-002 should replace it with real overview content. 3) MOCK_INVENTORY uses Math.random() seeded at build time — values differ between builds but are structurally correct. 4) All 15 CSS --db-* tokens added to globals.css without conflicting with --ob-* tokens. 5) DashboardSidebar uses `href.startsWith(pathname + '/')` for prefix-matching child routes — works correctly for all 10 nav items.
